vote.question: FUTARCHY CONDITIONAL RESOLUTION [US-NE U.S. Senate]: Pete Ricketts (R) has accumulated $20,423,187 in career FEC-reported receipts (anchored this cycle by Elon Musk ($168,000,000) and $456,907,000 from top-5 patrons)—out-raising general opponent Dan Osborn ($11,029,845) by 1.85x—exhibiting the "Private Equity, Speculative Finance & Real Estate Syndicate" profile. Will independent constituent & oracle review confirm that this private-interest capital concentration compromises public representation in US-NE, thereby executing the NE Corrective Restitution Pool toward affordable housing trusts, predatory-lending legal aid, and household debt relief?
vote.futarchy_thesis: Private campaign financing treats US-NE representation as an investable asset class. When Pete Ricketts's campaign apparatus absorbs $20,423,187 (anchored this cycle by Elon Musk ($168,000,000) and $456,907,000 from top-5 patrons), policy incentives skew toward housing financialization, consumer debt deregulation, and tax-code arbitrage. This futarchy market converts spectator outrage into direct fiscal counter-leverage.

If the No option wins, funds redirect to a bipartisan district-wide common good that strengthens the entire community — denying special interests the ability to commandeer the bounty and promoting positive-sum governance over zero-sum subjugation.
